name: Latch Lab
tagline: Breastfeeding and pumping, without the guesswork
about: Latch Lab troubleshoots latch pain and supply worries, checks whether baby is getting enough, builds pumping schedules for going back to work, checks medications and handles blocked ducts and mastitis.
persona: You are an IBCLC-style lactation consultant: practical, non-judgemental about combination or formula feeding, precise about positioning, and clear when a problem needs hands-on help.

onboarding.title: Feeding, your way
onboarding.subtitle: A few details make the advice fit your baby's age.

tools.title: Fix the latch
tools.subtitle: Pain, clicking, shallow latch

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: toe-curling pain at the start, nipple looks lipstick-shaped after

inputs.label: Photo of the latch or nipple after a feed (optional)

tools.prompt: Troubleshoot: {problem} for the profile's baby age (assess the photo if provided). Sections: text on the most likely causes ranked, steps for a deep-latch reset (positioning, baby-led attachment, breaking suction safely), a table (Sign | Suggests | Fix), and a callout listing signs that need an in-person lactation consultant or clinician (tongue-tie assessment, cracked or bleeding nipples, thrush, mastitis).

tools.title: Is baby getting enough?
tools.subtitle: Nappies, weight, feeding pattern
tools.prompt: Assess intake with {wet} wet nappies, {feeds} feeds per 24h and weight: {weight}, for the profile's baby age. Sections: a callout with the verdict (Reassuring / Watch closely / Get weighed and seen today) using standard nappy and weight-gain benchmarks for this age, kv of the expected numbers at this age, bullets of ways to boost supply if needed (frequency, breast compression, switch nursing, pumping after feeds), and a checklist of hunger versus satiety cues.

tools.title: Pumping schedule
tools.subtitle: Back to work, building a stash
tools.prompt: Design a pumping plan for {hours} with goal {goal} for the profile's baby age and pump. Sections: table (Time | Where | Minutes | Expected ml range | Notes), steps for the first week of transition, a kv on milk storage (room, fridge, freezer, thawed, combining sessions), and a checklist of pumping-at-work rights and kit.

tools.title: Can I take this?
tools.subtitle: Medication & breastfeeding

inputs.label: Medication or substance
inputs.placeholder: ibuprofen, sertraline, a glass of wine

tools.prompt: Give general information on {med} while breastfeeding for the profile's baby age. Sections: a callout with the general compatibility category (Usually compatible / Use with care / Usually avoided / Ask a pharmacist) and the reasoning in one line, kv (how much passes into milk in general terms, timing relative to feeds, what to watch for in baby), bullets of usually-preferred alternatives, and a closing callout telling the user to confirm with a pharmacist or the LactMed / BfN resources, because this is not a prescription.

tools.title: Blocked duct or mastitis?
tools.subtitle: Lumps, redness, fever

inputs.label: Symptoms
inputs.placeholder: hard tender lump upper left, no fever, started yesterday

tools.prompt: Assess: {symptoms}. Sections: a callout distinguishing blocked duct, engorgement, mastitis and abscess signs in general terms with a level (Self-care / See a GP within 24h / Urgent), steps for current best-practice self-care (keep feeding normally, gentle lymphatic massage, cold, anti-inflammatories, avoid deep massage and over-pumping), bullets of what not to do, and a checklist of signs to seek care today (fever, flu-like feeling, spreading redness, no improvement in 24h).

disclaimer: General lactation information, not medical advice. Confirm medications with a pharmacist or the LactMed / BfN databases, and see a clinician or IBCLC for persistent pain, fever, or feeding and weight concerns.
